newsitem.title: UK: Euro Products Outlook - weak as gasoline struggles.
newsitem.headline: Euro Products Outlook - weak as gasoline struggles.

text.p: European oil products look set for another bearish week with few signs of prices picking up in a significant way.
Gasoline is in the doldrums but prices may be supported by recent sales to the United States.
Two cargoes were sold on Friday but traders feel that arbitrage numbers are still not fully workable.

"They sold those cargoes just to get rid of them but to me the arb is totally closed," one European trader said. Prices need to sink by around $5 per tonne relative to U.S. prices before gasoline moves westwards in big quantities.
Prompt European gasoline is now weaker relative to August and September swaps because traders believe pre-U.K. July 2 budget buying is over, and prices look weak.
Prices in the Mediterranean are likely to fall and recent tightness, particularly for high octane barrels, is set to ease, dealers said.
Naphtha has eased, but there is room for further falls given the continued low price of gasoline.
Swaps prices for July have fallen to some $6 a tonne below those for gasoline and further weakness in gasoline may lead to an even greater supply of reforming barrels.
The outlook for high sulphur fuel oil barges is mixed.
"It all depends on who has interest in having prices up or down...Pricing, pricing, everything is related to pricing these days," one trader said.
Low sulphur barges should continue to be offered on the firm side, with at least four sellers at the $96 mark, the same level as the last deal last week. Buyers were a few dollars lower.

Views were mixed over high sulphur cargoes with some traders saying the market would be stable with Russian straight run offered at higher numbers, while others said it would be a bit weaker with some cargoes still on offer and not finding homes.

One percent was seen weakish with two cargoes to sell still not picked up. "I think one percent is going to come down. It stayed high but actually no deals were done," one seller offering at $94.50 fob said.
In the Mediterranean, traders said there was no real market for high sulphur straight-run while cracked may be pressured a little as the two buyers seen on the market were very relaxed.
Gas oil was expected to remain in the doldrums although barge market players said current low price levels might encourage some short-covering this week.
"The real question at the moment is at what point refiners will cut runs," one trader said.

Healthy margins have encouraged refiners to keep production at full capacity over the past few weeks, despite the generally poor level of demand. The over-supply situation has been further exacerbated by Mediterranean as well as some transatlantic material pouring into the region.

"As long as low sulphur material is over-supplied we're going to see buyers sitting on the sidelines waiting for premiums to sink lower." Some traders said the return to production by Dreyfus' 185,000 tonne Wilhelmshaven refinery at the end of June would also add to the supply glut.
